build: original disk, Rapidlok V6, PAL, C64 Preservation Project gunship_s1/s2[microprose_1985](rl6)(pal)

exclude: 3 parts: Debriefing, Flight, Side two loader
elsewhere: 3 parts: Debriefing, Flight, Side two loader

comments.text: The cartridge signature the KERNAL looks for on a reset: two vectors and the letters CBM80. A reset (and an NMI that reaches the KERNAL's handler) jumps through $8000 or $8002, here both $80DB, which blanks the screen and stops.
The letters CBM80 in PETSCII, with bit 7 set on the first three as the KERNAL's test expects.
Switches the ROMs and I/O out for a copy through any of memory: interrupts off, the processor port's setting saved into the operand at $8024 for rom_back to restore, then $01 = $04, all RAM.
SYS M6 (32788): rom_out, copy_up, rom_back. The copy reaches the RAM under the ROMs and the I/O.
SYS S6 (32797): rom_out, fill, rom_back. The fill reaches the RAM under the ROMs and the I/O.
Puts the processor port back as rom_out found it (its LDA operand is rewritten by rom_out) and turns interrupts on.
The operand of rom_back's LDA #: rom_out writes the processor port's setting here, so rom_back puts back whatever was there before the copy.
SYS SB (32809): stores the byte in $A5 into $AA whole pages and then $A9 more bytes, from the address in $A7-$A8. The BASIC sets $A5-$AA by POKE A0..A5.
SYS MV (32838): copies $AA pages and then $A9 bytes from the address in $A5-$A6 to the one in $A7-$A8, upwards.

SYS BM (32871): the same copy run backwards, from the last byte down, for a block that moves up over itself. $A5-$A6 and $A7-$A8 hold the last addresses; $A9 counts the bytes of the first pass and $AA the pages after it.

SYS KE (32910): calls a machine-code routine with registers set from BASIC. A from $A5, X from $A6, Y from $A7, the carry from bit 0 of $A8, and the routine's address in $A9-$AA. The loaders use it for the KERNAL's SETLFS, SETNAM and LOAD.

SYS 32921: colours the cockpit's window for the theatre, or for night. $A7 goes into five bytes ($3FC4, $420C-$420D, $422A-$422B), then $A5 fills 12 rows of 32 bytes from $402C and $A6 the same rows from $7C2C, 40 bytes to a row, the layout of a screen's colour cells. G2 calls it with four DATA values for each theatre.
Fills 12 rows of 32 cells with A, from the address in $A7-$A8, stepping 40 bytes a row.
Where a reset lands while the side two programs are in memory: the screen is blanked and the machine loops here for ever.
